human_review_checklist.item: No section headings in cover letter
human_review_checklist.note: Cover letter is flowing prose with no ## headers.

human_review_checklist.item: Cover letter has authentic opening hook
human_review_checklist.note: Opening 'I'm reaching out because your Applied AI team at Webflow is solving exactly the kind of problem I've spent three years obsessing over' sounds template-like and manufactured.

human_review_checklist.item: Company name and role appear naturally
human_review_checklist.note: Webflow and Staff Software Engineer, Applied AI appear naturally in context.
Role requires React, TypeScript, Node.js. Resume shows 'comfortable with TypeScript' but no Node.js or React proficiency demonstrated. These gaps are not acknowledged.

Phrases like 'solving exactly the kind of problem I've spent three years obsessing over', 'lights me up', and 'that's the part of this role that lights me up' read as AI-generated or template language.
Email and phone present in both resume and cover letter header.
Strong metrics: 50,000+ documents, 40% latency reduction, weeks-to-days improvement, 300+ users, 400+ consultants.
Resume and cover letter both use clean, consistent formatting.

strengths: Strong factual grounding with specific metrics: 50,000+ documents, 40% latency reduction, 'weeks to days' improvement
Resume bullets have measurable outcomes and concrete achievements
Clear AI/ML stack alignment: pgvector, Chroma, LangChain, Agents SDK, OpenAI
Role-appropriate experience: 3+ years in RAG and document intelligence
Education background shows continuous learning (Turing School backend engineering)
weaknesses: Gap handling FAIL: No React or Node.js skills demonstrated despite these being key requirements
Cover letter opening hook feels inauthentic - 'exactly the kind of problem I've spent three years obsessing over' reads as AI-generated
Template language in cover letter: 'lights me up', 'retrieval quality and user trust are the same problem' - too polished
Limited company specificity beyond surface-level Webflow observations ('millions of users', 'visual editor')
ATS keyword gaps: 'prompt engineering' not explicitly mentioned, no Node.js
Company name could be swapped out - content is generic enough to apply to many AI roles
Narrative voice feels slightly manufactured rather than conversational
revision_suggestions: Address the React/Node.js gap directly in cover letter: 'While my background is primarily Python, I've worked extensively in TypeScript environments and am eager to expand into React/Node.js work alongside your team'
Rewrite opening hook to be more specific and authentic - lead with the biopharma story instead of generic flattery
Remove or rework phrases like 'lights me up' and 'obsessing over' - they undermine authenticity
Add more Webflow-specific understanding: mention Webflow's visual editor, no-code platform, or recent AI features if genuine
Explicitly mention 'prompt engineering' as a skill since it's in the job requirements
Consider removing the Turing School mention - it may raise questions about formal CS credentials at Staff level
